items.summary: IBHVG2 heat-loss model structure (Black & Comenetz / Nordheim-Soodak-Nordheim + h0, thin shell, Newton cooling) and all $HEAT defaults (clean via ARL-TR-348 SI list) resolved; gauge (CLEN/NGAG/GLOC/GRAD) and $RES1 resistance inputs resolved; equations C.01-C.22 and D.16-D.27 are only partly legible in the OCR (D.18/D.21 errata illegible).

Resal/Taylor energy equation with M = [(1+theta)W + C/3]/g, theta = 0.05, heat loss via adjusted gamma (f ~ 0.15, larger in small arms), u = 17.5 and eta = 27.7 in3/lb; heat-transfer eqs 3-1..3-3 (lambda = (13.2 + 4 log10 d_cm)^-2, checked by worked example); Lagrange p(y) quadratic distribution from Hunt eqs 7,06/7,07/7,13 and Corner eq. 13. AMCP's own eqs 5-1..5-7 garbled.

Hunt sec. 6.10 and Corner sec. 10.41 Thornhill formulas located and partly transcribed (0.38, 0.6, C^0.8375, d^1.5, roughness 1.25 guns / 1.4+ small arms, eq. 41/42 checked); the d exponent in the denominator and Corner's H/theta exponents are illegible in the OCR.

Hunt 1951 Table 1.01 densities at 20 C: single-base 1.57-1.62 g/cm3 (NCT, NH, FNH/P), double-base cordites 1.54-1.61 g/cm3; AMCP generic 17.5 in3/lb = 1.58 g/cm3. 1940s gun propellants, not modern canister powders.

n: small-arms ball-propellant closed-bomb constant-exponent n = 0.8053 (Riefler & Lowery via Stiefel 1980; one OCR variant 0.8033); gun-propellant alpha 0.8-0.9 (AMCP), ~0.9 (Corner), per-propellant Hunt Table 5.01. K1: only artillery-oriented values (AMCP 1+theta = 1.05; Hunt 1.05 w + C/3; Corner rotation m 1.005-1.02); no small-arms K1 found.

records.topic: IBHVG2 energy-loss terms included in L(t)
records.reading: L(t) includes: projectile translational KE, translational KE of propellant and gases, projectile rotational KE, recoiling-barrel KE, work against barrel friction, work against air resistance in the tube, heat lost to the gun tube. Neglected: barrel deformation energy, work against propellant-bed friction / gas friction on the wall.
records.page_basis: printed page marker in OCR text at line 3345
records.evidence:
The term L(i) in (A.09) comprises the total work done by the interior ballistic system less
the energy transfered from the system at time t. In IBHVG2, L(l) includes contributions
from: the translational kinetic energy of the proj xtile, the translational kinetic energy of the
propellants and gases, the rotational kinetic energy of the projectile, the kinetic energy of the
recoiling barrel, work done against barrel friction, work done against the resistance of the air
in the tube opposing projectile motion, and heat lost to the gun tube. We neglect the amount of
energy expended in the deformation of the gun barrel and any work done in overcoming the
frictional resistance of the propellant bed or the combustion gases moving against the tube
wall.
